overview: Chiropractors treat problems of the spine, joints and muscles, mostly with hands-on adjustments. They take medical histories, examine posture and movement, order X-rays and give advice on exercise and lifestyle. O*NET rates knowledge of medicine at 4.83 out of 5 for this job and customer service at 4.66. Becoming one takes a Doctor of Chiropractic degree, about 4 years after college, and a state license. The BLS May 2025 median is $79,200 across 39,630 jobs. Many chiropractors run their own clinics, with freedom to set hours but long periods on their feet.
pay: Chiropractors earn a median of $79,200, but the range is wide: the lowest 10% earn under $43,460 and the top 10% $146,080 or more. New Jersey has the highest state median at $134,990, 70% above the national figure, followed by New York. Florida has the most chiropractors, 3,220.

faq.a: The BLS May 2025 median is $79,200 a year. The middle half earn between $60,070 and $105,050. Owning a practice usually means higher pay after a few years. New Jersey, New York ($120,950) and Maine ($107,300) pay the most, while Kansas and Utah pay the least.

faq.q: How long does it take to become a chiropractor?
faq.a: Most chiropractors complete a bachelor's degree or at least 3 years of college, then a Doctor of Chiropractic program of about 4 years. O*NET places the job in Job Zone 5. All states require passing national board exams and getting a license.

O*NET rates active listening and speaking at 4 out of 5 for this job, and critical thinking at 3.88. Knowledge of biology is rated 4.04 and therapy and counseling 3.96. Physical strength and good body mechanics matter, since adjustments are hands-on all day.

faq.q: What jobs are similar to chiropractor?
faq.a: The closest moves are Midwives (76% match), Athletic Trainers (73%) and postsecondary health specialties teachers (73%), based on O*NET 31.0. Health specialties teachers earn $107,310, 35% more, according to BLS May 2025, while Orthotists and Prosthetists, a 70% match, earn $81,110.
